TODDLER ROOM LESSON · TODDLER ROOM · AGES 1–3 YEARS

Laundry Basket — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches "laundry basket" through the in-and-out game toddlers are already obsessed with — and hides a real chore inside it, one garment at a time.

What is this?

A laundry basket is the woven container that holds the clothes — and, in this room, occasionally one giggling toddler.

What does it mean?

Containers are toddler physics 101: in, out, full, empty. The basket card meets the obsession head-on and borrows its momentum for tidying.

What does the child need to know?

You need the basket, a small pile of laundry on the floor and the one-piece rule: fetch ONE thing, drop it in, say what it was — "socks IN!" Repetition is the engine; the peekaboo is the dessert.

Why this matters

Chores at two are not chores — they are games with a finish line. The one-piece fetch is the smallest honest version of laundry day, and it counts.

What it teaches

In-out spatial concepts, carrying and dropping (aim!), item naming, following a repeated instruction, and the earliest work pride there is.

Words to learn

laundry basketinoutfetchsocksfull

Say this to your child

“"Laundry basket! The clothes go IN. Fetch one thing… the socks! Socks IN. Now the shirt… shirt IN. Towel IN! Look — the basket is FULL. And where is YOU? In the basket! Peekaboo!"”

Step by step

  1. Present the basket: "laundry basket! The clothes live here."
  2. Model one fetch: "socks — IN!" Drop with ceremony.
  3. Hand over the job: "your turn — fetch ONE thing!" One at a time; the count is the game.
  4. Name every landing: "shirt in! Towel in!" The basket fills; the vocabulary does too.
  5. The finale: "is anything ELSE left?" — and the toddler, if willing, climbs in. "IN the basket! Peekaboo!" Empty basket, full victory.

Look closer at the picture

On this card the words "laundry basket" sit under a blue woven basket — handles up, ready to hold the whole week’s wash.

Ask your child

"Where do the clothes go?" "Fetch ONE thing!" "Is the basket full or empty?"

What your child can say or do

Your child might say "IN!" on every drop, fetch items nobody asked for (enthusiasm!), or climb in before being asked — the schema demands it.

Out in the real world

Baskets live in every room: toy baskets, market baskets, the basket at the till. "That goes IN the basket!" scales the word to the whole house.

Try it together

Basket Post: the basket becomes a letterbox — toys "post" socks and clothes through the handles. Deliveries all afternoon; the laundry happens on schedule.

Understanding check

Ask: "What is this?" (laundry basket) "Put the socks IN!" "Full or empty?" — name, drop, fill: the container word is in.

This lesson pairs with the Laundry Basket flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Toddler Room.
